explanation: In a one-to-many relationship, the key from the one side goes into the many-side table as a foreign key. Here, one author can relate to many books, so `author_id` belongs in `Book`. The other choices either place the key on the wrong side or repeat author facts instead of implementing the relationship properly.

options.text: Store `author_id` in the `Book` table and keep author details in `Author`
Store `book_id` in the `Author` table and keep book details in `Book`
Store only `author_name` in the `Book` table and do not create an `Author` table
Store all author and book data in one table with repeated author rows

prompt: A bookstore tracks authors and books. One author can write many books, and each book has one author. Which table design correctly implements this one-to-many relationship?
reviewConcept: Place the one-side key in the many-side table to implement a one-to-many relationship.

source.section: Creating a database with a 1:m relationship
